findings.evidence: The passing importer closes and reopens inside one Node process only.
findings.counter_example: Process-local behavior can pass while a separately launched reader fails.
findings.repair: Call the evidence same-process close/reopen; require a fresh-process reader witness before stronger claims.

findings.evidence: Mixed string/Buffer normalization covers 55 lossless UTF-8 string inputs on the exact pairing.
findings.counter_example: Other input origins, versions, or malformed bytes can differ.
findings.repair: Pin the claim and add empty, large, multibyte, malformed, and non-string-origin fixtures.

findings.evidence: Expected records are checked, but absence of unmanifested extra keys is not proven.
findings.counter_example: Expected records plus stale malicious keys still pass.
findings.repair: Define expected-key closure separately from store-domain exclusivity; ignore extras as unreachable in L0 until reliable enumeration proves exclusivity.

findings.evidence: Removing writer methods gives logical immutability only; no OS/filesystem sealing is specified.
findings.counter_example: Another process mutates the directory after startup.
findings.repair: Rename to logically immutable and require OS read-only access or a sealed copy plus mutation detection before deployment.

findings.evidence: Evidence is one sequential writer then reader; no concurrent opens, locking, crash, or multi-reader proof.
findings.counter_example: Builder and service overlap on one directory and expose partial/corrupt behavior.
findings.repair: Claim no concurrency safety; prohibit overlap by construction and require separate-directory build, closed writer, fresh-process verify, external atomic selection, and adversarial tests.

findings.evidence: Startup expected-record checks do not cover malformed structures or post-start mutation/read exceptions.
findings.counter_example: Files change after readiness and later reads diverge.
findings.repair: On any read anomaly invalidate the whole handle, stop data routes, emit redacted diagnostics, and test tamper-after-open/malformed stores.

findings.evidence: Prepare/publish/drain is only narrative; no state machine, atomic pointer, rollback, or crash recovery exists.
findings.counter_example: Crash around publication leaves zero or two active generations.
findings.repair: Keep replacement outside L0; later specify prepare, verify, publish, acquire, drain, retire, rollback, and orphan cleanup.

findings.evidence: Fail-closed rebuild by another owner has no last-known-good, quarantine, retry, or readmission contract.
findings.counter_example: A corrupt new snapshot causes indefinite outage despite an older valid generation.
findings.repair: State L0 has no recovery beyond unavailability; assign and design recovery before deployment.

findings.evidence: One linux x64 Node 26.6.0 and @vijayee/wavedb 0.15.8 snapshot passed and denied integration admission.
findings.counter_example: Other filesystems, mounts, architectures, lifecycles, and workloads differ.
findings.repair: Keep the pairing as experimental evidence only; require an environment matrix for admission.

survived_attacks: 55 expected records had exact same-process reopen readback
request handle capture prevents intentional cross-handle composition
replacement and production remain outside proof
reroute: parent claim narrowing and design repair; executable experiments remain future SWUs
handoff_note: L0 consultation survives only as candidate design; same-process reopen, method restriction, and expected-key checks cannot become durability, immutability, concurrency, or exclusivity claims.
